Sen’s chat

The chat as it should be built: a full-height sheet over the screen it was opened from, drawn at true size in Minted, with dark and Copper where a second look matters. Your turn is a bubble; Sen’s is full width under one small line; what code builds sits in cards; the proposal is the one raised card.

3 · A table, and a figure’s sourceA table is a plain grid in the same card. Every figure in Sen’s words can be tapped: a thin underline says so. One that code couldn’t trace is dotted in the warning colour.

12 · The avatar’s journeyOne avatar with one home, its seat in the header. It leaves only for work or to wait on you, and it is never in two places. These are Minted’s own drawings, a still of each state.

RestingNothing runningSen is ready.
A new noteSen posted while you were awaySen has a note for you.
ListeningYou’re typingYou’re typing. Sen is ready.
WorkingFrom Send until the text starts, and while a proposal is appliedSen is reading your payments…
With helpersA subagent is runningSen is researching…
AnsweringText and parts are streamingSen is answering…
PausedWaiting on you; stopped; offline; out of credit; a step failedSen needs your answer.
DoneThe answer settled; 1.5 s, then restingSen has answered.

The journey of one answer, as a filmstrip · swipe sideways

What moves: one glide out, on Send. After that the avatar only follows the layout: down as parts land, onto a card that waits. Going home it doesn’t fly back over what you’re reading: it fades out there and in at its seat.

Reduced motion: no glide and no fade. The avatar cuts from place to place and holds one still frame per state, as drawn here.

Scrolled out of view, it shows in the jump-to-latest button instead (section 10), so it is still one avatar.

Either-or 3 · where the avatar rests · swipe sideways

The three either-ors, and my picks

1 · The head row (section 2): one line that is both the name and the source, over two lines. It keeps the verdict first.

2 · A question’s answers (section 5): rows that each say what they do, over chips with a paragraph.

3 · Where the avatar rests (section 12): at home in the header, over staying with the newest answer.

What I couldn’t make work as written, and what I drew instead

  1. Text in its own card. screens.md lists text among the parts that each get a card, and also says Sen’s turn has no bubble. A card round the words is a bubble, so Sen’s words are bare and only what code builds is carded. That is also what tells Sen’s words from code’s.
  2. An avatar in the header and one that travels. Both are decided, and only one avatar may exist. So the header is its home: it leaves for the conversation and its seat keeps a ring until it’s back.
  3. Jump-to-latest carrying the avatar’s state. Carrying it always would make a second avatar while Sen rests in the header. It carries the avatar only when the avatar’s place is out of view; otherwise it is an arrow.
  4. Done. The table has it play where the answer settled. Drawn at home instead, so the follow-ups don’t shift to make room for it.
  5. No way to edit a question is named, though an edited question makes a version. I added Edit to the long-press menu on your own message, where thumbs, Try again and Pin don’t apply.
  6. A menu holds two to five actions (D155), and a message’s has eight. The thumbs share one row and Delete is set apart, which leaves six rows.
  7. Chips are 32 px with a 48 px target. Wrapped onto two lines they need 16 px between the lines, not 8, or the targets overlap. Drawn at 16.
  8. The playground’s Apply (spec 12.3) shares a word with the proposal’s, but it only makes a proposal. Drawn small and outlined; I’d rename it Propose this.

Every phone is 390 × 844, scaled to fit the page; a strip is a piece of the chat at its true width. Inside them every colour, radius and font is the look’s token; the scrim, the shadows and the keyboard stand-in are plain black and grey, since a look has no token for them. The avatar is each look’s own drawing, saved as a still of each state. Names, amounts, banks and web pages are made up, on the same month the app’s screenshots use. Source: docs/ui/sen-chat/design-src/.
